label: Instagram
terms_note: Professional (Business or Creator) account required; free; two flavours — Instagram API with Instagram Login (graph.instagram.com; scopes instagram_business_basic, instagram_business_content_publish, messaging) and with Facebook Login for Business (graph.facebook.com; instagram_basic, instagram_content_publish, pages_read_engagement; adds hashtag search); App Review for non-tester users; 100 API-published posts per 24 h moving window (GET /{ig-id}/content_publishing_limit); BUC limit 4800 × impressions per 24 h; JPEG only for images; containers expire after 24 h — no server-side scheduling. Caution (docs read 2026-09-24): 'Advanced Access if your app serves Instagram professional accounts you don't own or manage; Standard Access if your app serves Instagram professional accounts you own or manage and have added to your app in the App Dashboard' (https://developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-platform/comment-moderation) - Advanced Access requires Meta App Review. 'Instagram accounts are limited to 100 API-published posts within a 24-hour moving period' (content-publishing).

endpoints.purpose: 100 API-published posts per 24 h moving window

reference.limits: - 100 API-published posts / 24 h per account (carousel = 1); BUC limit 4800 × impressions per 24 h. - No shopping tags, no filters, JPEG only; no server-side scheduling — the platform scheduler must hold the post. - Free; Meta Platform Terms; App Review + (for some permissions) business verification.

fields.name: access_token
fields.help: Instagram API with Facebook Login (host graph.facebook.com): a User or Page access token from Facebook Login for Business for a person with a role on the Facebook Page linked to the Instagram professional (Business or Creator) account, with instagram_basic, instagram_manage_comments, pages_read_engagement (and pages_show_list); sent as `Authorization: Bearer` (https://developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-platform/comment-moderation).

config_fields.name: ig_user_id
config_fields.help: Instagram professional account id (IG User id, e.g. 17841405822304914) - GET /{page_id}?fields=instagram_business_account returns it. me and read_mentions call /<ig_user_id>. Env: PLATFORM_MCP_INSTAGRAM_IG_USER_ID.

me.note: GET /{ig_user_id}?fields=id,username,name,followers_count,media_count ('Get fields and edges on an Instagram Business or Creator Account').

read_comments.note: GET /{ig_media_id}/comments: 'Returns only top-level comments', 'Returns a maximum of 50 comments per query', 'Comments cannot be filtered by timestamp'; results are reverse chronological. page/limit are not sent (cursor paging).

reply_comment.note: 'To reply to a comment, send a POST request to the /<IG_COMMENT_ID>/replies endpoint ... with the message parameter set to your message text'; answers {id} of the new comment (instagram_manage_comments).

read_mentions.note: GET /{ig_user_id}/tags: 'IG Media objects in which an IG User has been tagged by another Instagram user' (private media are not returned). `since` goes to posted_after (ISO 8601, strict bound; 'This filtering capability is rolling out gradually'). Caption @mentions without a photo tag come only through the `mentions` webhook + mentioned_media / mentioned_comment lookups, which need the ids from that webhook. Cursor paging: page/limit are not sent.

analytics_post.note: GET /{ig_media_id}?fields=id,like_count,comments_count,permalink,timestamp,media_type (IG Media fields; like_count 'is omitted if the media owner has hidden like counts' when read indirectly). Reach / views / saves come from GET /{ig_media_id}/insights?metric=..., not used here. The runtime cannot compose a nested `metrics` object, so counts are top-level fields.

not_offered.publish_text: Instagram has no text-only post: 'In order to publish a media object, it must have a container' created with image_url or video_url (https://developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-platform/content-publishing).
not_offered.publish_image: Two calls: 'send a POST request to the /<IG_ID>/media endpoint' with image_url to create a container, then 'Send a POST request to the /<IG_ID>/media_publish endpoint with ... creation_id set to the container ID' (https://developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-platform/content-publishing); the runtime makes one call per tool.
not_offered.delete: The IG Media reference documents reading only; DELETE is documented for IG Comments (DELETE /<IG_COMMENT_ID>, https://developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-platform/instagram-graph-api/reference/ig-comment), not for published media.
